blogs.title: Beyond Type 1 and Type 2: Why Every Young Adult with Diabetes Needs a MODY Probability Check
blogs.description: This post explores the diagnostic trap of misclassifying monogenic diabetes. We will analyze why this patient, despite having a BMI of 24.6 and features resembling metabolic syndrome, was actually suffering from HNF1A-MODY. The discussion will focus on the utility of the Exeter MODY calculator versus local epidemiology, emphasizing that 'atypical' features (like a relatively high BMI or co-existing dyslipidemia) do not rule out MODY, and advocating for genetic testing when clinical suspicion exists.

blogs.title: The Renal Threshold Clue: Unmasking HNF1A-MODY via Glycosuria Out of Proportion to Glucose
blogs.description: Focusing on a specific pathophysiological hallmark of HNF1A-MODY, this article discusses the unique combination of hyperglycemia and profound glycosuria caused by defective SGLT2 expression in the proximal tubule. We will review how to interpret urinalysis in young diabetics where urine glucose exceeds what one would expect from plasma glucose levels alone, serving as a red flag for renal handling defects characteristic of HNF1A mutations.

blogs.title: From Insulin to GLP-1: Precision Pharmacotherapy in HNF1A-MODY Beyond Sulfonylureas
blogs.description: While sulfonylureas remain the classic first-line therapy for HNF1A-MODY due to their mechanism on ATP-sensitive potassium channels, this post examines modern alternatives like GLP-1 receptor agonists (e.g., dulaglutide) and DPP-4 inhibitors. Using the case patient's successful transition off insulin to GLP-1 agonism followed by oral agents, we will discuss when to avoid sulfonylureas (hypoglycemia risk) and how newer drug classes can offer comparable efficacy with improved safety profiles in preserving beta-cell function.

blogs.title: Novel Variants and ACMG Criteria: Interpreting 'Unknowns' in Next-Generation Sequencing Reports
blogs.description: Addressing the complexity of genetic diagnostics, this educational piece dives deep into the interpretation of the novel c.809A>G (p.N270S) variant found in this patient. Since it was absent from major databases like ClinVar, we will walk through how clinicians and geneticists apply ACMG guidelines—using AlphaMissense scores, structural domain location (DNA-binding domain), and familial segregation—to classify a variant as Pathogenic/Likely Pathogenic despite its novelty.

blogs.title: The Hidden Danger: Why SGLT2 Inhibitors May Be Contraindicated in HNF1A-MODY Patients
blogs.description: This cautionary post highlights a critical medication mismatch. Because HNF1A mutations naturally downregulate SGLT2 expression leading to renal glycosuria, adding an SGLT2 inhibitor can precipitate severe dehydration or euglycemic DKA by further inhibiting glucose reabsorption. We will contrast this with standard T2D protocols where SGLT2is are often preferred, urging clinicians to verify MODY status before initiating sodium-glucose cotransporter inhibitors.
